article_title: Crystal 1.22.3 Patches Four Newly Disclosed Vulnerabilities, Including an HTTP Request-Smuggling Desync Bug and a Port-Truncation SSRF Bypass
summary: Submission approved with corrections: all facts, PR numbers, quotes, and figures verified against raw source snapshots except one severity-label misquote.

findings.message: Article quotes severity as "medium" for GHSA-6q3x-6xhw-wfxp and GHSA-5425-p3gq-r48v; GitHub's advisory pages label both "Moderate", not "Medium".
findings.details: Checked source-3.html.gz (GHSA-6q3x-6xhw-wfxp) and source-2.html.gz (GHSA-5425-p3gq-r48v): both pages display the severity badge text "Moderate". The article's body_markdown says 'Two of the advisories carry a "medium" severity rating,' using quote marks that imply verbatim source terminology. This is a subordinate specific (not in headline/summary/lead) and is being filed as a correction rather than a rejection.

content_preview.title: Crystal 1.22.3 Patches Four Newly Disclosed Vulnerabilities, Including an HTTP Request-Smuggling Desync Bug and a Port-Truncation SSRF Bypass
content_preview.summary: Crystal's November 13 patch release fixes four GitHub security advisories covering an HTTP chunked-encoding desync, a socket port-truncation SSRF bypass, an Enum.parse? stack write, and an IO::Delimited boundary bug.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Crystal programming language project released version 1.22.3 on November 13, 2026, a patch the [official release announcement](https://crystal-lang.org/2026/11/13/1.22.3-released/) says ships "important security patches, regression fixes, and normal bug fixes." Alongside the release, the project [published](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/security/advisories/GHSA-5425-p3gq-r48v) four GitHub Security Advisories the same day, covering issues in the standard library's socke...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece: an Overview establishing the release and advisory count, a section walking through all four GHSA advisories grouped by severity, a section on the three further security-tagged fixes that didn't get separate advisories, and a 'What We Don't Know' closer. Technical details (port truncation math, byte-offset desync, buffer-boundary peek bug) are explained accurately and accessibly. 817 words, within the News 400-1200 range.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 7 source snapshots from disk (gunzip'd sources/2026-11/crystal-1223-patches-four-newly-disclosed-vulnerabilities-including-an-http-request-smuggling-desync-bug-and-a-port-truncation-ssrf-bypass/source-{0..6}.html.gz) and verified each decompressed file's sha256 matches manifest.json (all 7 matched). All 7 fetched with status_code 200, no archive_fallback, no suspicious_patterns. source-0 (crystal-lang.org blog): confirmed 'important security patches, regression fixes, and normal bug fixes', the 14-changes/4-contributors stat, the TCPServer.new(73616) example, and all three HTTP-parser-hardening bullet points (PRs #17903, #17898, #17902) plus the exact quoted framing sentences. source-1 (GitHub release tag 1.22.3 changelog): confirmed PR numbers #17848, #17898, #17916 each appear exactly once, tagged under 'security' (7 occurrences of the word). source-2 (GHSA-5425-p3gq-r48v): confirmed severity badge reads 'Moderate' (not 'Medium' as quoted in the article), CWE-787, Patched versions: 1.22.3 (the only one of the four with this field populated), finder credit Blacksmoke16, patch PR #17836. source-3 (GHSA-6q3x-6xhw-wfxp): confirmed severity badge 'Moderate', Patched versions: None, affected/not-affected target lists verbatim, the glibc-2013-ticket quote verbatim ('doesn't seem to be considered a vulnerability'), the 73616->8080 reproduction example, reporter credit bararchy, patch PR #17848. source-4 (GHSA-j97w-qwpv-7cfv): confirmed severity 'Low', Patched versions: None, byte positions 14 vs 24 (10-byte gap) verbatim from the PoC, reporter bararchy, patch PR #17898. source-5 (GHSA-jgv7-2p84-pm39): confirmed severity 'Low', Patched versions: None, the 'We are not aware of any immediate vulnerability...' quote verbatim, reporter bararchy, patch PR #17916. source-6 (GHSA-wqh5-7w63-pm68): confirmed title 'Crystal HTTP::Server is prone to request smuggling', published Apr 16 2026, Patched versions: 1.20.0 - matches the article's framing of this as an earlier, separate round of request-smuggling fixes. One discrepancy found and filed as a correction: the article's quoted severity label 'medium' for two advisories does not match GitHub's actual label 'Moderate' on those pages. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is Crystal/GitHub security advisories; Anthropic/Claude is not the subject and is not mentioned in the article body.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked against raw snapshot text: CVE absence ('No known CVE' on all 4 advisories, confirmed), the patched-versions asymmetry (only GHSA-5425 lists 1.22.3; the other three list 'None', confirmed), all PR/advisory cross-references, the glibc bug-tracker characterization, the byte-offset proof-of-concept numbers, the CWE classifications (CWE-787, CWE-20/CWE-197, no-CWE x2), and the internal link to the prior Crystal 1.22.0 article (file exists at src/content/articles/2026-10/15-crystal-1220-published-october-12-removes-processfork-exits-on-broken-pipe-writes-and-moves-aarch64-linux-to-tier-1.md, and does not mention these four issues, consistent with the article's claim). The lone inaccuracy is the 'medium' vs. 'Moderate' severity-label misquote described above; it is a subordinate specific, not in the headline/summary/lead, and does not affect the article's central claims.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and precise throughout. Attributions are carefully scoped ('the advisory calls', 'the announcement frames', 'a count the project reports itself rather than one independently verified by the Herald'). No sensationalism despite the headline combining 'request-smuggling' and 'SSRF bypass' - both terms are the advisories' own characterizations, not editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Crystal 1.22.3 or these four advisories. The only related prior article, Crystal 1.22.0 (2026-10-15), covered a different release and is correctly cited as not mentioning these since-disclosed issues. Genuinely new topic.
concerns: Article quotes severity as "medium" (in quote marks, implying verbatim sourcing) for two advisories that GitHub's own pages label "Moderate" - filed as a correction, see corrections record.
recommendations: Future submissions should quote GitHub Security Advisory severity labels verbatim (Low/Moderate/High/Critical) rather than substituting a synonym inside quote marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced News coverage of a routine but legitimate patch release with four real security advisories; every PR number, byte offset, quote, and structured field (patched-versions, CVE, CWE, credits) was independently verified against the raw GitHub/crystal-lang.org snapshots and matched. One isolated, subordinate severity-label misquote ('medium' vs. the source's actual 'Moderate') is being corrected via a public corrections record rather than blocking publication, since it doesn't touch the headline, summary, or lead and the underlying technical substance is unaffected. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine patch-release coverage for a niche language's security-conscious developer audience, accurate but not broad-impact or exceptional.
